children: TOKYO, October 1 (Reuters) - Foreign investors remained netsellers of Japanese stocks for the week ending on September 26, capital flows data showed on Thursday.    Foreigners sold a net 362.0 billion yen worth of shares inthe week through Sep. 26, after selling a net 4,942.5 billion yenin the week before that.    Japanese investors sold a net 684.5 billion yen of foreignbonds in the latest week after selling a net 1,904.9 billion yenthe week before.    Details of net investments were as follows (in billion yen):

FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN JAPAN:    (net)                                       stocks         bonds        bills    September 20 - September 26        -362.0      -1,341.8     -3,267.2     September 13 - September 19      -4,942.5         -84.3     +1,251.1     September 6  - September 12      -1,520.4r     +2,240.2r    -1,212.8
JAPANESE INVESTMENT ABROAD:    (net; a minus sign indicates net selling and inflows of funds into Japan)

stocks         bonds        bills    September 20 - September 26        +225.8        -684.5       +130.9     September 13 - September 19         +44.3      -1,904.9       +344.5     September 6  - September 12        +157.4r     +1,091.0r      +150.8     August 30 - September 5            -478.8r       +114.0r      +107.1

Notes:    - An "r" denotes a revised figure.    - Bonds include beneficiary certificates.    - Figures are based on contracts and are rounded.    - The MOF's capital flows data can be found in English at:    http://www.mof.go.jp/international_policy/reference/itn_transactions_in_securities/week.pdf
